name: Moldova
summary: The Neamț ethno-folklore area is situated in the central-northern part of Moldova. Representative villages: Agapia, Tâmpești. Bucovina, which became the Duchy of Bucovina in the Austrian Empire, is a historical region comprising a territory of 10,443 km² covering the area adjacent to the cities of Cajvana, Câmpulung Moldovenesc, Gura Humorului, Frasin, Milișăuți, Rădăuți, Siret, Solca, Suceava, Vatra Dornei, and Vicovu de Sus in Romania, as well as Chernivtsi, Kitsman, Zastavna, Vashkivtsi on Cheremosh, Vyzhnytsia, Sadhora, and Storozhynets in Ukraine. The region is also at the crossroads between Eastern Europe and Central Europe. Vrancea is a county in the historical regions of Moldova and Muntenia, Romania. The county has an area of 4,863 km², and the capital is the municipality of Focșani. The main watercourses are: Siret, Șușița, Putna, Milcov, Râmnicu Sărat. The highest altitudes are the Lăcăuț and Goru peaks. Vrancea County is bordered to the northeast by Vaslui County, to the east by Galați County, to the southeast by Brăila County, to the south by Buzău County, to the west by Covasna County, and to the north by Bacău County. The county is located between the geographical coordinates 45°23’ and 46°11’ north latitude and 26°23’ and 27°32’ east longitude, being situated in the southeastern part of the country, at the curvature of the Eastern Carpathians.
